findings.claim: M1 and M2 still allow missing or altered review evidence to erase blockers despite a structured summary being present.
findings.evidence: M2 checks the record summary only. cmd_artifact_review stores counts in record['findings'] but stores dispositions separately in evidence. _blocking_finding_fingerprints reads that evidence and uses "except (OSError, ValueError): return []". Thus deleting or corrupting the evidence produces the same fingerprint set as zero blockers; editing its findings also changes progress without another governed review. reserve_evidence explicitly promises that 'a reader that needs it refuses it as malformed'. The type filter does not repair this. Both _loop_progress and cmd_loop_show's gate summary consume this helper; review_status and gate review_precondition consume ledger results without validating these findings.
findings.suggested_fix: Validate the selected review evidence and its correspondence to the ledger before consuming findings; refuse missing, malformed or inconsistent evidence instead of returning an empty set. Add tests covering progress recording and gate summary, and explicitly document the boundary for detecting edits to otherwise valid evidence.

findings.claim: The in-flight guidance overlooks iterations whose unstructured review step was already recorded: they can finish without encountering M2 and cannot simply record a replacement review.
findings.evidence: M-PLAN says "An in-flight loop's next review step must add --findings". cmd_loop_step persists "findings": review.get('findings'), currently allowing None. cmd_loop_record only requires the last step to be 'trace', then calls implementation_ready and _loop_progress; it does not revalidate the recorded review's structure. loop_output_precondition permits review output only when the last step is 'manifest', so an iteration already past review cannot record the prescribed replacement. M2 at the review branch therefore leaves the original defect reachable across an upgrade.
findings.suggested_fix: Specify and test an upgrade policy for iterations already past an unstructured review: refuse completion and provide an engine-supported restart/recovery route, or explicitly grandfather them and narrow the integrity claim. Do not prescribe hand edits to runtime records.

findings.claim: The proposed agent-only rule conflicts with the stated human-waiver contract and leaves the actor policy unresolved for implementation.
findings.evidence: M3 proposes refusal only for '--actor-type agent'; §4 leaves tool/test/system as an open question. PLAN Appendix C says "After M, a waiver requires a review recorded with --actor-type human". REVIEW_ACTOR_TYPES includes human, agent, tool, test and system, and cmd_artifact_review accepts structured findings for every review type. Consequently tool/test/system can record blocking accepted findings under the proposed rule. The assertion that refusing all non-human actors would break reviews 'that never mark accepted today' does not follow: those reviews would not trigger the refusal. ADR-007 §3 correctly treats caller identity as convention; it does not resolve this operational inconsistency.
findings.suggested_fix: Choose one rule before implementation and align both plans and prompts. To satisfy Appendix C, refuse blocking accepted findings for every actor type except human, across all review types, before reserve_evidence (which creates a placeholder). Test all five actor types and both PASS and FAIL, while retaining the self-declaration limitation.
